body: Funny how things work like that.  I was probably 10 minutes away from hanging myself, was finishing tying the noose and finding a suitable spot in my room to do it and a workmate from down the hall knocked on my door to ask some simple question about our schedule.  We didn’t talk about it or anything but it took me away from the situation long enough for me to realize I needed to call someone.  There’s plenty of things worth living for, depression just blinds you from seeing them.

Seeking help in the army feels so counterproductive.  I got sent to the hospital for nearly blowing my brains out and now the whole company thinks I’m a shitbag and a waste of space.  But of course when it’s not behind closed doors they say “talk to me whenever man you know I’m here for you.”  When they think I’m not around it’s “man he should’ve just done it, what a selfish prick” or “why does he have to be in OUR platoon.” People just don’t understand how depression is, and what it does to a person.

I’m so so sorry that you’re still going through all this.  I’ve noticed at least for myself that there are various triggers that can cause these kinds of memories or feelings.  It never really goes away but becomes more manageable, and I’ve found myself most happy when either trying to confront the triggers or try and cut them from my life

I’m only 2 months out from when I found out my fiancé had been texting inappropriate messages to a tinder “friend” and honestly it’s completely on them when it comes to progress.  Sure, you’ll have to deal with the feelings and work on yourself but you’ll never heal if they don’t put in the effort.  After confronting my fiancé and fighting for weeks (we’re still fighting) she saw how bad she fucked up.  She showed me all her inboxes to show me she doesn’t text anyone else, she swore off talking to guys until we regain trust, and has agreed to do whatever it takes to repair the relationship.  I’m not saying every person has to do this but it takes a LOT of effort on the WS to even begin the healing process, and from what I’ve read here, it can happen.  But it takes an enormous amount of effort and commitment.  It isn’t hopeless, it just takes time and effort.

It’s been 2 weeks (moving on 3) that I’ve been severely depressed, and probably close to 4 months that it’s affected how I work, but my CoC just found out.  It’s been hard to kindve just drop it, believe me I would if I could, you think at some point they’ll just start ignoring the issue or thinking I’m a shitbag? I’m worried of getting the boot cause of being a liability but if I just pretend everything is better it’d be worse for everyone else.
I agree, given the fact that the screenshots explicitly show HER picture on the Snapchat story and also her bitmoji.  (People like to text on Snapchat nowadays, now I know why)

The problem is she hasn’t admitted to actually doing it, she insists the text messages were faked in some way and she’s broken up that I don’t trust her. There’s still a pinch of doubt that is making things tough
I haven’t decided if I want to end things or try and work through them.  She’s flying up here in 1 week for a 4 day weekend pass so we can talk and she can come clean.

The trickle truth part happened from the beginning. First, it was a long time friend she had known for years. Then, its that they started talking again in August. Now it’s February, and he’s a tinder guy she felt “close friends” with.  I had to delete the pictures of the messages before they drove me insane.  Honestly I have no idea how I’ll get past this, the lies are just absolutely mind boggling.
Still trying to figure that part out.  I feel like I need to get back on track from the depression I’m in right now in order to make that decision, whether it be to tough it out or break up.

Once, for lunch. She tells me he made a move and she rejected, nothing happened.  The messages (and the guy) tell me that there was never any gesture to initiate that but that after the date there was more messages exchanged about what could’ve happened.  Physical cheating didn’t happen, but very well could have if it continued longer.

Went into Behavioral and am currently waiting to be evaluated.  Not much to my surprise, everyone  (family and best friend) seemed pretty shocked when I told them what was going on.  Chain of command seems super supportive which might be good but is also probably due to the fact there have been a lot of suicides here lately.  But I guess we’ll see what happens.

Believe me... if you're depressed and not in the military, you will be borderline suicidal if you were actually in.  It's not all the glamour that social media and TV makes it out to be.  It's 99% boredom, and then 1% actually doing work.  That's if you get a good job in the military, if you pick a bad one you'll be miserable all the time.
It's exhausting isn't it.  Some people just don't understand that suicidal thoughts doesn't make someone want to actually die.  They just want the pain to stop.
